answer: An agent market requires every bidding identity to lock a separate $100 bond, whether its job is writing a sonnet or selecting velvet cushions for a window ledge. Each bond stays locked while the identity is active and for 30 days afterward; the same funds cannot support several identities. An attacker fielding 1,000 fake bidders must therefore immobilize $100,000, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital.
